newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader out to change face of Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader out to change face of Africa.

text.p: Laurent Kabila opposed President Mobutu Sese Seko for 32 years. Here are some quotes from Kabila during his eight-month rebellion that toppled the Zairean leader:

"Why support a government that has pillaged the country, ruined the country, a government of thieves. They have mansions everywhere. No money finds its way into the people's pockets." (November in Goma)

"Why should Rwanda, a country which has been attacked by Mobutu, not be one of our friends? For me, it is sympathetic to our cause. I would not be surprised if Uganda was sympathetic after incursions by rebels based on Zairean territory." (February in Goma)
"Did you allow the Nazi party and the Italian fascists to take part in elections after World War Two? So why should you expect the alliance to share power?" (April in Mbuji-Mayi)
"This rebellion is not only about changing this country, it is about changing the face of Africa." (March in Kisangani)
"My long years of struggle were like spreading fertiliser on a field. But now it is time to harvest." (March in Goma)
"If the French come (to prop up Mobutu), we shall bury them." (March in Goma)
"There is no parliament. It is illegal. There have never been elections. Everything is illegal. The Mobutu regime was a militarist regime." (May in Launda, Angola)
"They (the United Nations) blame the refugee problem on me as if I am in charge of it. These are mainpulations because they want to force us to accept compromises." (May in Lubumbashi)

"I hope the French position (against the rebels) will change. We are really democrats. What represents our hope is that we have the capacity to modernise this country. France needs this country, which is one of the biggest francophone countries." (May in Lubumbashi)
"The United States is doing a very good job with Mr Mobutu. They have been making him conscious of the dangers he may face if he insists on clinging to power unnecessarily." (May in Lubumbashi)
"I told Mobutu 'Resign. You have no more power. You have failed and it's finished'." (May in Lubumbashi after their first face-to-face meeting on a South African navy ship)
"I pity Mobutu...but there was no need for me to shake his bloody hands." (May in Lubumbashi)
